terra.problem: “Ears first and hands second” turns the contrast between listening and the sacrifice of fools into an order for listening and acting.
The verse says to listen rather than offer the sacrifice of fools. It does not say listening is the first job at the house of God.
The oven agreeing about fulfilling a vow has no clear connection to the teaching, so the joke does not land.
Calling a vow a mistake is described as a “way out,” adding an intention the text does not give.
The verse does not say the person is trying to talk their way out of the vow.
The verse does not say the person would call the vow a mistake to wiggle out of it.
“That question is really there” adds little beyond repeating the answer. The explanation feels generic rather than like Papa Dorin.
The Teacher says to let your words be few, not that he wants them to be short and plain.
The passage warns against hasty speech and many words, but that is not necessarily the opposite of speaking boldly.
